title: Δάμαλις καὶ βοῦς
part: The Heifer and the Ox (Chambry 92 · Perry 300)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 92 (= Perry 300). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Δάμαλις βοῦν ὁρῶσα ἐργαζόμενον ἐταλάνιζεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῷ κόπῳ.
sentences.tr: Damalis boun horōsa ergazomenon etalanizen auton epi tōi kopōi.
sentences.l: A heifer, seeing an ox working, kept calling him wretched for his toil.
sentences.n: ταλανίζω is to call someone τάλας, wretched — to pity aloud, not to help. The imperfect ἐταλάνιζεν makes it a habit rather than a single remark, and ὁρῶσα is present: she watches while he works. ἐπί with the dative gives the ground of a feeling.

sentences.t: Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἑορτὴ κατέλαβε, τὸν βοῦν ἀπολύσαντες, τὴν δάμαλιν ἐκράτησαν τοῦ σφάξαι.
sentences.tr: Epeidē de heortē katelabe, ton boun apolysantes, tēn damalin ekratēsan tou sphaxai.
sentences.l: But when a festival came upon them, having loosed the ox, they laid hold of the heifer for the slaughtering.
sentences.i: But when a festival came round, they let the ox go and took hold of the heifer to cut her throat.
sentences.n: The subject of the plural verbs is never named — the farm's people; Greek leaves it to be inferred. τοῦ σφάξαι is an articular infinitive in the genitive expressing purpose. σφάζω is to cut the throat of a victim, the sacrificial word. The ox is spared because he works: the festival needs a beast, and the idle one is the one that can be spared.

sentences.t: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ βοῦς ἐμειδίασε καὶ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· « Ὦ δάμαλις, διὰ τοῦτο ἤργεις διότι ἔμελλες ἀρτίως τυθῆναι. »
sentences.tr: Idōn de ho bous emeidiase kai pros autēn eipen· « Ō damalis, dia touto ērgeis dioti emelles artiōs tythēnai. »
sentences.l: And the ox, having seen it, smiled and said to her: « O heifer, for this reason you were idle, because you were going presently to be sacrificed. »
sentences.i: And the ox saw it, smiled, and said to her: « Heifer, this is why you were idle — because you were shortly to be sacrificed. »
sentences.n: διὰ τοῦτο … διότι points forward to its cause and then supplies it: 'for this reason … namely because'. ἤργεις is the imperfect of ἀργέω, to be ἀργός, idle. τυθῆναι is the aorist passive infinitive of θύω, again the verb of sacrifice: her leisure was the leisure of an animal kept for the altar.

sentences.t: Ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ ὅτι τὸν ἀργοῦντα κίνδυνος μένει.
sentences.tr: Ho mythos dēloi hoti ton argounta kindynos menei.
sentences.l: The fable shows that danger awaits the one who is idle.
sentences.n: μένω with an accusative is transitive, 'to await, to lie in wait for': danger is the subject and the idler the object. The present participle τὸν ἀργοῦντα is generic — whoever is idle, at any time.
